steps.say: This video explains retrieval-augmented generation: an application retrieves passages for each question, and a language model answers from them.
A language model answers from its prompt. For a large collection, the application selects passages for each question.
The passages come from a vector store, prepared beforehand from the documents as chunks with metadata and vectors.
This pattern is called retrieval-augmented generation, or RAG.
steps.speak: This pattern is called retrieval-augmented generation, or rag.

steps.say: In this example, a user asks how internet access and economic development have evolved in Rwanda and Kenya.
The search returns four passages. The answer draws on them and cites a passage after each figure.
Its opening line states that the passages contain no economic indicators.
A correct answer needs four figures for 2024, and the store holds all four.
steps.speak: A correct answer needs four figures for twenty twenty-four, and the store holds all four.

steps.say: The four passages in the prompt hold the two figures on internet use.
The model reads only its prompt, so the figures on GDP per capita cannot appear in the answer.
steps.speak: The model reads only its prompt, so the figures on G D P per capita cannot appear in the answer.

steps.say: The embedding model of the store turns the question into a vector of 384 numbers.
steps.speak: The embedding model of the store turns the question into a vector of three hundred eighty-four numbers.

steps.say: Cosine similarity compares two vectors by the angle between them. A score of 1 means identical meaning, and 0 means unrelated.
steps.speak: Cosine similarity compares two vectors by the angle between them. A score of one means identical meaning, and zero means unrelated.

steps.say: Every one of the 21 chunks in the store receives a score, and the chunks are ranked by it.
steps.speak: Every one of the twenty-one chunks in the store receives a score, and the chunks are ranked by it.

steps.say: The search returns the top k, here four, as the passages for the prompt.
steps.speak: The search returns the top kay, here four, as the passages for the prompt.

steps.say: Each passage enters the prompt under a citation built from its metadata: the document, the section, and the year.
The passages and the question form the user message. The grounded instructions form the system message.
The model writes from these two messages and places a citation after each figure.
For the two-part question, three internet chunks and a note on mobile money take the four places.
The first economy chunk is fifth, at 0.570 against 0.591 for the fourth. The section on GDP per capita in Kenya is ninth.
steps.speak: The first economy chunk is fifth, at zero point five seven zero against zero point five nine one for the fourth. The section on G D P per capita in Kenya is ninth.

steps.say: A k of nine would include it, with the note on coffee in seventh place. Each added passage costs tokens in every call.
steps.speak: A kay of nine would include it, with the note on coffee in seventh place. Each added passage costs tokens in every call.

steps.say: The fix runs one search for each part and merges the results. The eight merged passages hold all four needed figures.
A vector holds nothing about the date of its text. A second question asks for the latest available figures, with k set to two.
steps.speak: A vector holds nothing about the date of its text. A second question asks for the latest available figures, with kay set to two.

steps.say: The 2016 summary ranks first at 0.816, because its text uses the same phrase. The Kenya brief misses the cut-off, so the answer gives 16.6 percent, for 2015.
steps.speak: The twenty sixteen summary ranks first at zero point eight one six, because its text uses the same phrase. The Kenya brief misses the cut-off, so the answer gives sixteen point six percent, for twenty fifteen.

steps.say: Rewording the question in the vocabulary of the newer briefs raised the score of the summary to 0.871. The summary stayed first.
steps.speak: Rewording the question in the vocabulary of the newer briefs raised the score of the summary to zero point eight seven one. The summary stayed first.

steps.say: A filter on the date in the metadata keeps documents from 2020 or later. Both country briefs are then returned, and the answer gives 35.0 percent for Kenya in 2024.
steps.speak: A filter on the date in the metadata keeps documents from twenty twenty or later. Both country briefs are then returned, and the answer gives thirty-five point zero percent for Kenya in twenty twenty-four.

steps.say: A search always returns k chunks. For the population of Rwanda, the section on population ranks first at 0.739.
steps.speak: A search always returns kay chunks. For the population of Rwanda, the section on population ranks first at zero point seven three nine.

steps.say: The collection holds nothing on inflation in Uganda. The search still returns three sections on GDP per capita, the best at 0.534.
steps.speak: The collection holds nothing on inflation in Uganda. The search still returns three sections on G D P per capita, the best at zero point five three four.

steps.say: A cut-off on the score between the two would stop the weak passages. Its value depends on the embedding model and is set from examples.
The grounded instructions add a second safeguard: the model says when the passages do not answer.
With one search for each part, the answer covers internet use and GDP per capita, with a citation after each figure.
steps.speak: With one search for each part, the answer covers internet use and G D P per capita, with a citation after each figure.

steps.say: The citation of the Kenya figure for GDP per capita leads to its section, which states 2,133 US dollars for 2024.
steps.speak: The citation of the Kenya figure for G D P per capita leads to its section, which states two thousand one hundred thirty-three U S dollars for twenty twenty-four.

steps.say: Retrieval can be tested without the model. Each test question lists the documents and numbers that a correct answer needs.
With four passages per question, an expected document is among the passages for all eight questions.
The main question finds two of its four needed numbers, with no call to the model.
When both checks pass and an answer is still wrong, the fault lies in generation.
Tests check the passages, and the grounded instructions make the model cite them and report gaps.
Whether a passage fits the question remains a judgement for the builders of the application and for the reader.
The citation helps that judgement. Its year shows at once that the regional summary dates from 2016.
steps.speak: The citation helps that judgement. Its year shows at once that the regional summary dates from twenty sixteen.
